bull.t: Exceptional TPV growth and merchant retention
bull.b: Rapid TPV growth combined with strong retention indicates that DLocal is expanding both its merchant base and share of wallet within existing relationships. This supports durable revenue scaling because merchants are adding countries, payment methods, products and verticals through the platform.

A broadening regulatory footprint and deeper local payment connectivity strengthen DLocal’s ability to serve global merchants across complex emerging markets. These capabilities can raise entry barriers, support geographic expansion and improve the platform’s long-term usefulness to multinational customers.

bull.t: Strong recent profitability and cash generation
bull.b: Strong operating and free cash flow, closely aligned with net income, indicate that recent profits are converting into financial resources rather than remaining largely accounting-based. This supports continued investment in technology, licensing and products while preserving balance-sheet flexibility.

bear.b: The multi-year decline in gross and net margins shows that strong growth has not translated proportionally into profitability. Continued margin pressure could reduce the earnings benefit of higher payment volume and constrain the funds available for product development, expansion and shareholder returns.

DLocal’s growth model currently combines rising TPV with declining take rates, creating a risk that incremental volume produces less profit. Persistent pricing pressure and elevated processing costs, especially in Mexico, could make it harder to stabilize margins as the platform scales.

bear.t: Uneven cash-flow profile and rising leverage
bear.b: Recent cash generation is strong, but the prior negative cash-flow period demonstrates that working-capital or timing effects can make internally generated funding uneven. At the same time, rising leverage reduces the company’s historically more conservative financial profile and flexibility.
